Every one of the 32 restore steps consumes the remainder produced by the previous step, so the chain is a strict data dependency: no logic_restructure, tree rebalancing or mux flattening can make it shallow, and the residual ALU logic on the path (the result case-mux and the zero compare) is only a few ns of the 156.8. The one transform that does fit an 849-level dependency chain is pipeline -- cutting the divider into, say, 4 stages of 8 restore steps -- but that requires a clock and a valid/busy handshake inside alu, and alu's port list (src_a, src_b, alu_control, alu_result, zero) has no clk and may not be changed under the stated rules; the stage registers cannot be hidden in div_restoring_32 either, because alu has no clock to hand it.
